intent: A sound quiz on a map: three loudness bars that put a monkey in second place, an erased 'A ROAR' that becomes a click, a pin on the Norwegian canyon where it was measured, and a depth counter dropping 2 kilometres into the dark.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: What is the LOUDEST animal on Earth?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: What is the loudest animal on Earth?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: Blue whale, Howler monkey, or Sperm whale?
The sperm whale. Its clicks reach 236 decibels underwater, the loudest sound any animal makes.

lines.direction: ease back over the Norwegian Sea; three decibel bars rise on 'blue' with the whale towering; the monkey sticker on 'howler'; the 5 KM card and an ear sticker on 'heard' as Norway pulses
lines.text: A blue whale call hits 188. A howler monkey, loudest on land, about 140, heard 5 kilometres off.

lines.direction: drift north along the coast; the A ROAR plate waits at the bottom and wipes away on 'roar'; a stopwatch sticker on 'click'; a nose sticker on 'nose' as Norway pulses
lines.text: Not a roar. Each click lasts a fraction of a millisecond, fired from the whale's enormous nose.

lines.direction: tighten on the Vesterålen coast; the Andenes pin and tag on 'measured'; a squid sticker on 'squid'; the depth counter runs 0 → 2,000 metres on 'squid'; a moon sticker on 'dark' as Norway pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Measured off northern Norway. The whales hunt squid 2 kilometres down, in the dark, by sound.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: The loudest voice is a click. Follow us.
